note: Write-path vectors hand-authored from SPEC.md prose, as opposed to gen/stamp.json, which is emitted from the reference for breadth. The first nine are SPEC.md §3.3 (v1.5): text inside a fenced code block is content, so a writer must not put a marker there, must not rewrite a marker-shaped string already there, and must still let the fence itself carry a stay in the ordinary way. The read-path half of the rule is in spec/parse.json and spec/lint.json. The rest are SPEC.md §5.3's write refusal (v1.11): a leading `---` span that recognition rejects only because its YAML-ish payload holds a blank line is still YAML to a frontmatter reader, so a writer inserts no marker on its lines and mints no stay for a block that starts on them, while what follows the closer is stamped as usual and a marker already in the span is refreshed in place. Recognition is unchanged: spec/parse.json's frontmatter-payload-with-a-blank-line-is-content still reads that span as content.

vectors.name: stamp-refuses-a-span-whose-blank-line-is-a-form-feed
vectors.note: SPEC.md §5.3 (v1.11): the write refusal's blank line is blank in §5's ASCII sense, so a payload line holding only a form-feed (U+000C) is blank and the span is refused like `stamp-refuses-to-write-into-yaml-with-a-blank-line`: only `Body.` is stamped. A writer that counted only spaces and tabs as blank would find no blank line here, take the span for something else, and insert markers on lines 2 and 5.
